title: Regulatory Change, Digital Transformation and Decarbonization Take Center Stage at the 40th Hellenic Marine Technical Committee
summary: The 40th Hellenic Marine Technical Committee convened, ostensibly to discuss "decarbonization" and evolving regulations like the EU ETS, alongside IMO's Net-Zero Framework. Bureau Veritas presented "technical innovation" and "operational excellence" via digital solutions, yet offered no concrete plans for immediate shifts away from high-carbon HFO usage. Such discussions often prioritize compliance strategies and perceived efficiency gains over tangible, absolute emission reductions, allowing continued high carbon intensity despite looming FuelEU Maritime fines.
content:

From emerging environmental regulations to advances in digital technologies, maritime stakeholders are navigating a rapidly evolving landscape. These challenges and opportunities formed the focus of discussions at the 40th Hellenic Marine Technical Committee, held on 20 November at the Grand Hyatt Hotel in Athens, where Bureau Veritas specialists shared insights into the trends shaping the future of shipping.

The meeting opened with welcome remarks from George Sarris, Chairman and President of Enterprises Shipping & Trading S.A., followed by an address from George Andreadis, Bureau Veritas M&O Greece, Malta and Cyprus Director. The opening session also included the election of new committee members.

The morning program focused on the evolving regulatory landscape and the strategic challenges facing shipowners. Discussions covered the latest developments following IMO and EU meetings, including updates on the Net-Zero Framework and the revision of the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). Participants also examined the impact of China’s continued shipbuilding expansion across all major vessel segments and explored the growing importance of cybersecurity as the maritime industry accelerates its digital transformation.

Following a networking break, the afternoon session turned to technical innovation and operational excellence. Presentations highlighted advances in remote inspection techniques and digital survey solutions, developments in marine shaft alignment, and updates to VeriSTAR Green. Together, these discussions demonstrated how technology, engineering expertise and data-driven solutions are supporting safer, more efficient and more sustainable shipping operations.

Dedicated Q&A sessions throughout the day encouraged active exchanges between committee members and Bureau Veritas specialists, providing a valuable opportunity to discuss both current industry challenges and emerging trends. The event concluded with a cocktail reception, allowing participants to continue conversations and strengthen connections across the maritime community.

Through discussions spanning regulation, digitalization and technical innovation, the committee provided participants with practical insights into the challenges and opportunities shaping the future of shipping, while reinforcing the importance of industry dialogue in a period of rapid change.

A milestone edition of the committee, the event once again demonstrated the value of knowledge sharing and collaboration in helping the maritime sector navigate an increasingly complex operating environment.
